content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2: overtime, a short break shift, chat deflection and callback on general, with no agents moved from payments. Predicted 81.3% overall SL at ₹10,872.","why":"The extra calls come from the 09:00 loan email (MKT-2026-551), not from a staffing shortfall. Over the last four intervals there were 307 calls against 236 forecast, driven by loan_enquiry and new_offer_enquiry, and SL fell to 68% at 09:45. R2 adds capacity with overtime for 22 agents (10:45-12:45), then 16 (12:45-14:00), then 5 (14:00-15:00). It also delays general breaks 10:15-10:45 by 30 min, deflects 20% of new_offer_enquiry to chat, and turns on IVR callback for general. It is the cheapest option that meets the 80% target with no policy breaches. Predicted results are 81.3% overall SL (general 78.2%, payments 84.0%) and abandons down to 4.0% from 7.5% if no action is taken.","trade_offs":["Cheaper plans all fall short or break policy. No action leaves SL at 69%. P1 costs nothing but only reaches 68% and pushes payments below its 70% floor. P2 reaches 75.4% for ₹360 but relies on a known-issue message with no confirmed incident.","P4 hits 80.0% for ₹4,140 but uses the same IVR outage message for a marketing campaign, which breaks CX-01.","P3 costs ₹9,810, ₹1,062 less than R2, but reaches only 79.9% and drops payments to 52% during the 11:00-12:00 move.","R1 adds a safe 2-agent move and reaches 81.8% (3.9% abandons), but costs ₹810 more than R2 for a small gain.","Keeping all payments agents in place protects payments (84.0%). General still sits slightly under target at 78.2%, so the 80% is met at the overall level rather than on each queue."],"watch":"Confirm overtime uptake by about 10:30. R2 depends on roughly 22 agents accepting, and a shortfall will leave general below 78%. Track loan_enquiry and new_offer_enquiry volumes against the campaign surge, and check callback backlog after 14:00. If general SL stays under about 75% by 11:00, revisit R1's 2-agent move."}
